anomalies.observed: On the Water Level Sensor/Switches sheet, PR1 LiDAR is drawn connected to the main +5V rail and to the main I2C bus via H1/P1 (I2C_SDA and I2C_SCL), and H1 pin 5 is also labeled EZO_PDIS. The same EZO_PDIS net is used on the I2C Sensors sheet to connect U3 pin 8 and U4 pin 8, and on the SoC sheet to ESP32 pin IO6/SPI_CLK.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that PR1 is excluded from the board, its pins are typed free, and it is not wired into any net. EZO_PDIS is intended only to tie U3 pin 8 and U4 pin 8 to the ESP32 isolator-disable GPIO.

evidence.quote: Water Level Sensor/Switches: PR1 LiDAR connected to +5V, I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL, GND, and EZO_PDIS via H1/P1.
PR1 ... its pins are "free" ... it is not wired into any net.
An EZO_PDIS net ties both U3 pin 8 and U4 pin 8 ... to a single ESP32 pin.

anomalies.impact: If PR1 is populated, the isolator power-disable GPIO is tied to a LiDAR UART/enable pin, creating output contention and possible damage or undefined isolator control; the LiDAR also adds an unexpected device to the I2C bus even though firmware does not use it.

anomalies.observed: On the Power Train sheet, the board LDO U2 AZ1117-3.3 output VO is connected to the global +3V3 rail, and the ESP32-C6 DevKit internal 3.3 V LDO symbol M1B also has its 3V3 output connected to the same +3V3 rail.
anomalies.expected: The specification identifies U2 as the 5 V to 3.3 V LDO whose VO feeds the board +3V3 rail. A second regulator output (the DevKit's internal LDO) should not be tied directly to the same rail without isolation or an explicit parallel-regulator design.

evidence.quote: Power Train: U2 AZ1117-3.3 VO to +3V3; M1B ESP32-C6-DEVKIT 3V3 to +3V3.

anomalies.impact: Two 3.3 V regulator outputs are paralleled. Depending on tolerances and load, one regulator can back-feed or sink current from the other, causing thermal stress, instability, or damage to the DevKit's onboard regulator.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows at least two deviations from the intended r2 design: the TF-Luna LiDAR PR1 is wired to the I2C bus and to the EZO_PDIS control net despite being specified as not wired, and the board 3V3 rail is driven by both U2 and the DevKit's internal LDO M1B.
